gen_risks.description: Escalation of South Sudan conflict leading to a surge in refugee influx that overwhelms public services and natural resources in host districts.
gen_risks.mitigation: Coordinate closely with OPM, UNHCR, and local authorities to adjust WSS capacity plans and prioritize flexible, scalable infrastructure in refugee-hosting districts.
gen_risks.evidence: continuation of this conflict could affect export earnings and place an excessive amount of pressure on Uganda’s public services and natural resources.

gen_risks.description: Limited domestic contracting capacity leading to non-responsive bids or substandard execution of complex water infrastructure works.
gen_risks.mitigation: Package contracts appropriately, perform market sounding, encourage joint ventures, and widely disseminate bidding opportunities to attract capable international contractors.
gen_risks.evidence: limited capacity of domestic contractors to conduct projects of this nature, complexity, and scope

gen_risks.description: Social friction or resistance when transitioning refugees from free emergency water provision to a paid tariff structure.
gen_risks.mitigation: Implement community sensitization programs, introduce pro-poor progressive tariffs, and collaborate with OPM and UNHCR on refugee water policy design.
gen_risks.evidence: given that refugees in settlements currently do not pay for water, the UNHCR and OPM are collaborating with the MWE on designing a new water tariff policy

gen_risks.description: Failure to operationalize the IFMS project module at MWE resulting in accounting errors and inaccurate project financial reports.
gen_risks.mitigation: Fully operationalize the IFMS project module at MWE and maintain dedicated qualified financial management specialists within the Project Support Team.
gen_risks.evidence: the project module of the IFMS has not been fully operationalized at the MWE, which increases the risk of errors and inaccuracy of financial reports

gen_risks.description: Prolonged internal approval processes causing significant delays in vendor payments and potential contractor claims.
gen_risks.mitigation: Establish a transparent payment approval tracking system and hold approving officers accountable to streamline internal approval workflows.
gen_risks.evidence: delays in paying vendors due to prolonged internal approval processes

gen_risks.description: Financial non-viability of service providers (NWSC and UWAs) due to high operating costs in newly transferred small towns.
gen_risks.mitigation: Implement automatic cost-indexing tariffs, professionalization contracts, solar pumping conversions, and efficiency enhancement programs to lower unit costs.
gen_risks.evidence: small towns that are or will be part of the NWSC’s service area have higher than average operating costs.

gen_risks.description: Inefficiencies across procurement processing stages causing severe schedule slippage in contract awards.
gen_risks.mitigation: Engage experienced procurement specialists in the PST, train Procurement Disposal Unit staff on WB procedures, and enforce strict procurement tracking timelines.
gen_risks.evidence: inefficiency in processing, causing delays at each stage of the procurement cycle

gen_risks.description: Construction delays and cost overruns stemming from initial cost underestimation and poor contractor performance.
gen_risks.mitigation: Complete detailed engineering designs before procurement, establish comprehensive contract management plans, and enforce active on-site supervision.
gen_risks.evidence: delayed construction and underestimation of the cost of works

gen_risks.description: Incomplete needs assessments and inadequate geotechnical investigations leading to major design variations during execution.
gen_risks.mitigation: Conduct rigorous geotechnical studies, complete baseline needs assessments, and perform thorough design reviews prior to issuing bidding documents.
gen_risks.evidence: incomplete needs assessments and inadequate attention to geotechnical studies leading to design changes/variations during implementation

gen_risks.description: Seasonal low flows in Namatala River failing to meet projected Mbale water demands while threatening minimum environmental flows.
gen_risks.mitigation: Conduct an Augmented Water Supply Study prior to construction to implement source protection, water impoundment, or borehole augmentation options.
gen_risks.evidence: Namatala’s dry weather flows in some cases may not be sufficient to meet projected water demand and maintain an adequate EF.

gen_risks.description: Failure to regularly share internal audit review reports with the World Bank, reducing fiduciary oversight and assurance.
gen_risks.mitigation: Enforce mandatory quarterly submission of internal audit reports to the World Bank and monitor follow-up actions through the MoFPED Audit Committee.
gen_risks.evidence: ministry internal audit review reports are not shared regularly with the World Bank

gen_risks.description: Gaps in contract management capacity and high staff turnover leading to poor supervision of complex civil works.
gen_risks.mitigation: Provide specialized training on FIDIC contract management, retain key PST personnel, and deploy qualified supervising engineers full-time on site.

gen_risks.description: Inadequate physical office space and record storage for PDU staff leading to poor documentation control and audit risks.
gen_risks.mitigation: Provide dedicated lockable filing space, upgrade physical archiving facilities, and mandate digital document management via STEP.
gen_risks.evidence: limited office space for PDU staff and inadequate storage capacity for procurement records

gen_risks.description: Increased climate variability, extreme rainfall, and droughts damaging water infrastructure and destabilizing raw water yields.
gen_risks.mitigation: Integrate climate-resilient engineering standards, implement buffer zone protection, catchment afforestation, and real-time hydrological monitoring.
gen_risks.evidence: increased temperatures would produce higher levels of potential evapotranspiration... intense precipitation that is likely to lead to damaging and life-threatening floods

gen_risks.description: Improper handling and disposal of hazardous Asbestos Cement (AC) pipes during rehabilitation works posing occupational and public health hazards.
gen_risks.mitigation: Enforce strict AC pipe management procedures following NEMA guidelines, including proper PPE, safe containment, specialized transport, and controlled disposal.
gen_risks.evidence: improper handling of asbestos cement (AC) pipes, OHS risks

gen_risks.description: Disturbance or habitat degradation of hippopotamus populations during construction and operation of the Busia Water Treatment Plant.
gen_risks.mitigation: Consult Uganda Wildlife Authority and enforce a site-specific Wildlife Management Plan to protect hippopotamus habitats during civil works.
gen_risks.evidence: impact on hippopotamus at the WTP site was identified as a key impact that needs to be adequately mitigated

gen_risks.description: Labor influx into local communities causing social disruption, potential gender-based violence (GBV), and spread of communicable diseases.
gen_risks.mitigation: Mandate worker codes of conduct, prioritize local labor hiring, establish labor camp management plans, and conduct community sensitization on GBV/HIV.
gen_risks.evidence: management and monitoring of labor influx to minimize any potential GBV in Project areas

gen_risks.description: Long travel distances to unimproved water sources exposing women and children to heightened risk of gender-based violence and harassment.
gen_risks.mitigation: Construct localized piped water supply systems and community water points within 200m walking distance to eliminate long travel times.
gen_risks.evidence: Long walks to water sources trigger serious social consequences, including GBV, such as sexual assaults of women and girls

gt_risks.description: Political and governance risk: as detailed in the CPF, significant political uncertainty is not foreseen, but governance and effective public-sector management present substantial risks.
gt_risks.mitigation: The Project will mitigate these risks through (a) strengthening the MWE's regulatory framework; (b) carrying out a citizen engagement strategy; and (c) strengthening project implementation efforts in close coordination with local government officials and development partners. The World Bank's procurement processes will also help safeguard the Project from corruption.

gt_risks.description: Institutional capacity for implementation and sustainability risk: the Umbrella Water Authority (UWA) as a regional service delivery model for small towns and RGCs was recently introduced. Although the decision to scale up this model was informed by extensive analytical work and a pilot project, the UWA model was only recently operationalized.
gt_risks.mitigation: The Project will support implementation of a professionalized monitoring system focused on enhancing revenue collection approaches (billing software, cashless/mobile payment systems) and on strengthening integration of specialized private operators through improved contract management. The implementation team will use the Utility Performance Monitoring and Information System (UPMIS) tool to regularly review UWA and NWSC performance.

gt_risks.description: Fiduciary risk: the Procurement risk is rated Substantial while the FM risk is Moderate. The risks identified relate to delays and skills gaps at different stages of procurement processing.
gt_risks.mitigation: IWMDP will benefit from the lessons learned and mechanisms put in place under the predecessor project (WMDP); detailed mitigation measures for the procurement risk are set out in the Appraisal (Procurement) section.

gt_risks.description: The environmental and social risk is deemed Substantial given (a) potential opposition to the introduction of a new service delivery model, including new tariffs and catchment management measures; (b) the influx of new workers in small towns and RGCs; and (c) potentially adverse environmental impacts from the construction and operation of the proposed investments.
gt_risks.mitigation: The environmental and social risk will be managed through the application of an Environmental and Social Management Framework (ESMF), a Resettlement Policy Framework (RPF), and related safeguards instruments (Environmental and Social Impact Assessment, Resettlement Action Plans).

gt_risks.description: Other risks (social tensions in districts hosting refugees): tensions between refugees and citizens are caused by inequity in access to and payment for water supply and sanitation (WSS) services. While refugees in the settlements benefit from humanitarian aid and GoU support, Ugandans in host communities receive limited support for services and infrastructure, causing social tension that may result in Project implementation delays given potential community opposition to the works.
gt_risks.mitigation: The GoU has prioritized development efforts for poor districts hosting refugees while remaining firmly committed to its policy on refugee protection. The Project will manage this risk by designing WSS facilities and catchment management measures that benefit both host communities and refugees, and by ensuring the Project's social and communication management plan is applied and adequately supervised. There are no known existing risks to the refugee protection framework or reputational risks for the Project.
